verdicts.reason: Both use the same structure: the headline is pushed high with a tight top margin, and the subline and CTA are squeezed into one bottom row. The subline is tiny there and the CTA pill sits close to the right and bottom edges, which leaves the layout top-heavy and the centred axis of the original broken. A's headline breaks awkwardly ('botanicals and / a little / sunshine.'), leaving a ragged two-word line. B breaks it more naturally ('botanicals / and a little / sunshine.') and its CTA is slightly larger, so B is marginally better.
